patch_description:
This replaces the wide beam search with a single long-horizon simulated-annealing walk specialized for the sliding-puzzle state graph.

For every legal slide, the solver evaluates the resulting board immediately. It uses the official largest-tree size as the dominant objective, while also using the number of graph components and total matched edges as smoother secondary signals. At high temperature it deliberately accepts inferior moves to leave local optima; as the search progresses it increasingly chooses the strongest neighbor. A bounded recent-state tabu set prevents short loops, and periodic reheating restores exploration if progress stalls.

Unlike the prior implementation, this does not retain, sort, hash, and copy thousands of full board states at every depth. This makes each iteration cheap enough to spend nearly the whole move budget on an adaptive trajectory, while retaining the best prefix ever seen as the output.
